hints: Factorise $\sec^4\theta - \tan^4\theta$ as a difference of two squares.
Apply the Pythagorean identity $\sec^2\theta = 1 + \tan^2\theta$ to simplify the expression to $1 + 2\tan^2\theta$.
walkthrough:
Express the left-hand side as a difference of two squares:
$$\sec^4\theta - \tan^4\theta = (\sec^2\theta - \tan^2\theta)(\sec^2\theta + \tan^2\theta)$$

Recall the standard trigonometric identity $\sec^2\theta = 1 + \tan^2\theta$, which implies:
$$\sec^2\theta - \tan^2\theta = 1$$

Substitute this into the factored expression:
$$(\sec^2\theta - \tan^2\theta)(\sec^2\theta + \tan^2\theta) = (1)(\sec^2\theta + \tan^2\theta) = \sec^2\theta + \tan^2\theta$$

hints: Substitute the identity from part (a) with $\theta = 2\alpha$ into the equation.
Form a quadratic in $\tan^2(2\alpha)$, solve for $\tan(2\alpha)$, and find all angles in $0^\circ < \alpha < 180^\circ$.
walkthrough:
Apply the identity from part (a) with $\theta = 2\alpha$ to replace the left-hand side:
$$\sec^4(2\alpha) - \tan^4(2\alpha) = 1 + 2\tan^2(2\alpha)$$

Equate this to the right-hand side and substitute $\sec^2(2\alpha) = 1 + \tan^2(2\alpha)$:
$$1 + 2\tan^2(2\alpha) = 2\tan^2(2\alpha)\sec^2(2\alpha)$$
$$1 + 2\tan^2(2\alpha) = 2\tan^2(2\alpha)(1 + \tan^2(2\alpha))$$
$$1 + 2\tan^2(2\alpha) = 2\tan^2(2\alpha) + 2\tan^4(2\alpha)$$

Determine the principal basic angle for $2\alpha$:
$$\beta = \arctan(0.8408964) \approx 40.062^\circ$$

Find all values of $2\alpha$ in the range $0^\circ < \alpha < 180^\circ \implies 0^\circ < 2\alpha < 360^\circ$:
- From $\tan(2\alpha) = +0.8408964$ (quadrants I and III):
  $$2\alpha_1 = 40.062^\circ \implies \alpha_1 \approx 20.0^\circ$$
  $$2\alpha_3 = 180^\circ + 40.062^\circ = 220.062^\circ \implies \alpha_3 \approx 110.0^\circ = 110^\circ$$
- From $\tan(2\alpha) = -0.8408964$ (quadrants II and IV):
  $$2\alpha_2 = 180^\circ - 40.062^\circ = 139.938^\circ \implies \alpha_2 \approx 70.0^\circ$$
  $$2\alpha_4 = 360^\circ - 40.062^\circ = 319.938^\circ \implies \alpha_4 \approx 160.0^\circ = 160^\circ$$

State all four solutions rounded to 1 decimal place (or 3 significant figures):
$$\alpha = 20.0^\circ, 70.0^\circ, 110^\circ, 160^\circ$$
